data-index-in-node="0">Select: Business</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="4,0,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="4,0,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Why:</b> The Facebook Messenger API is only available for <b data-path-to-node="4,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="54">Business</b> apps.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,0,1,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Capability:</b> Business type apps are required to generate the <b data-path-to-node="4,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="60">access tokens</b> needed to bridge the logic from Make.com to Messenger.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,0,1,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,0,1,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Access:</b> This type is specifically designed for managing a presence and utilizing messaging features across Meta's technologies.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Avoid: Consumer</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="4,1,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="4,1,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,1,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Why:</b> Consumer apps cannot generate the necessary access tokens for this kind of integration.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,1,1,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,1,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Limitation:</b> If you select Consumer, you will not see the Messenger product options required for the bridge.</p></li></ul></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="5"><b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="0">The 11.3% Move</b></h3><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="6"><li><p data-index-in-node="6">Next</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,2,0">On the next screen (App Details), name the app <b data-path-to-node="6,2,0" Generate the Page Token (Box 2)</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="7"><li><p data-path-to-node="7,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Connect Page:</b> Click the blue <b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="29">"Connect"</b> button under the "No FB pages yet" section.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="7,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Select Ziggy's Page:</b> Select the Facebook Page you created for this identity and follow the prompts to continue.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="7,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Generate Token:</b> Once connected, a <b data-path-to-node="7,2,0" data-index-in-node="34">"Generate Token"</b> button will appear. Click it, copy the code, and <b data-path-to-node="7,2,0" data-index-in-node="100">save it in a secure note immediately</b>. Meta will not show this code again.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="8"><b data-path-to-node="8" data-index-in-node="0">3. This means Ziggy will only respond to messages sent by <b data-path-to-node="11" data-index-in-node="98">you</b> (the Architect). Watch Messages</b> bubble).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="8,2,0">In the settings for that bubble, you must select the <b data-path-to-node="8,2,0" data-index-in-node="53">Ziggy_Bridge</b> webhook from the dropdown menu.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="8,3,0"><b data-path-to-node="8,3,0" data-index-in-node="0">Crucial:</b> Once linked, right-click that module and select <b data-path-to-node="8,3,0" data-index-in-node="57">"Run this module only."</b> It will say "Waiting for data." <b data-path-to-node="8,3,0" data-index-in-node="113">Do not close this tab.</b></p></li></ol><h4 data-path-to-node="9"><b data-path-to-node="9" data-index-in-node="0">Step 2: Connect the Voice in Meta</b></h4><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="10"><li><p data-path-to-node="10,0,0">Go back to your <b data-path-to-node="10,0,0" data-index-in-node="16">Facebook Developer</b> dashboard (the screen from image 11).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="10,1,0">In <b data-path-to-node="10,1,0" data-index-in-node="3">Section 2 (Generate access tokens)</b>, click the blue <b data-path-to-node="10,1,0" data-index-in-node="54">"Connect"</b> button.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="10,2,0">A popup will appear. To link the <b data-path-to-node="1" data-index-in-node="156">Ziggy_Bridge</b> to a scenario and wake up the brain, follow these exact taps:</p><h3 data-path-to-node="2"><b data-path-to-node="2" data-index-in-node="0">1. Finding the "Scenarios" Tab (Make.com Mobile)</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="3"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">The Purple Bar:</b> Look at the very top of your screen for the purple menu bar.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">The Hamburger Menu:</b> Tap the <b data-path-to-node="3,1,0" data-index-in-node="28">three horizontal lines</b> in the top-right or top-left corner.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Select Scenarios:</b> In the vertical menu that slides out, tap the icon that looks like a circle with lines connecting to other circlesâ€”this is the <b data-path-to-node="3,2,0" data-index-in-node="145">"Scenarios"</b> tab.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,3,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,3,0" data-index-in-node="0">Click Your Scenario:</b> You should see the one you were building (likely named "New Scenario" if you didn't rename it). Tap it to open the bubble editor.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="4"><b data-path-to-node="4" data-index-in-node="0">2. Linking the "Ghost" Webhook</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="5"><li><p data-path-to-node="5,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="5,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Tap the Messenger Bubble:</b> Once the editor opens, tap the <b data-path-to-node="5,0,0" data-index-in-node="57">Facebook Messenger</b> module (the "Watch Messages" trigger).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="5,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="5,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Choose Webhook:</b> In the settings popup, look for the "Webhook" field. Tap the dropdown and select the <b data-path-to-node="5,1,0" data-index-in-node="101">Ziggy_Bridge</b> hook you already created.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="5,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="5,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Save:</b> Hit <b data-path-to-node="5,2,0" data-index-in-node="10">Save</b> or <b data-path-to-node="5,2,0" data-index-in-node="18">OK</b>.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="6"><b data-path-to-node="6" data-index-in-node="0">3. Activating the "Ear" (The Handshake)</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="7"><li><p data-path-to-node="7,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Run Once:</b> At the bottom of the scenario editor, tap the blue <b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="61">"Run once"</b> button. The Messenger bubble will start spinning and say <b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="129">"Waiting for data"</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="7,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Switch to Meta:</b> While it's spinning, jump back to your <b data-path-to-node="7,1,0" data-index-in-node="55">Facebook Developer</b> tab.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="7,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Finalize:</b> Hit the <b data-path-to-node="7,2,0" data-index-in-node="18">"Verify and Save"</b> button in Section 1.</p></li></ul><blockquote data-path-to-node="8"><p data-path-to-node="8,0"><b data-path-to-node="8,0" data-index-in-node="0">Operational Warning:</b> If you don't hit "Run once" in Make <i data-path-to-node="8,0" data-index-in-node="57">first</i>, Facebook's ping will fail because no "Scenario" is active to receive the signal.</p></blockquote><p data-path-to-node="9"><b data-index-in-node="79">Ziggy_Bridge</b> you already created.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Add the "Brain" (The Gemini Module)</b>:</p><ul data-path-to-node="3,2,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,1,0,0">Click the small <b data-path-to-node="3,2,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="16">(+)</b> icon on the right side of the "Brain."</p><h3 data-path-to-node="1"><b data-path-to-node="1" data-index-in-node="0">Step 1: Configure the Gemini Brain</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="2">Open the settings for your <b data-path-to-node="2" data-index-in-node="27">Google Gemini AI</b> module (the one shown in your last image) and fill in these specific fields:</p><ul data-path-to-node="3"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">AI Model</b>: Tap the dropdown and select the latest available model, such as <b data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">System Instructions</b>: Tap <b data-path-to-node="3,1,0" data-index-in-node="25">"Add a System Prompt"</b> under the System Instructions section. Paste the persona directive here:</p><blockquote data-path-to-node="3,1,1"><p data-path-to-node="3,1,1,0"><i data-path-to-node="3,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">"You are Ziggy, the Sentinel Node. ADHD-pattern processing. Baseline 11.3%. Direct, non-linear, intellectually honest. This tells Gemini to process the actual text you sent to the Page.</p></li></ul></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="4"><b data-path-to-node="4" data-index-in-node="0">Step 2: Add the Response Module</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="5">To make Ziggy talk back, you need to add a third bubble at the end of the line:</p><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="6"><li><p data-path-to-node="6,0,0">Tap the small <b data-path-to-node="6,0,0" data-index-in-node="14">(+)</b> icon on the right side of the Gemini bubble.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,1,0">Search for <b data-path-to-node="6,1,0" data-index-in-node="11">Facebook Messenger</b> and select the <b data-path-to-node="6,1,0" data-index-in-node="45">"Send a Message"</b> action.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Recipient ID</b>: Map the <b data-path-to-node="6,2,0" data-index-in-node="22"><code data-path-to-node="6,2,0" data-index-in-node="22">Sender ID</code></b> field from the very first Facebook Messenger bubble. This ensures the message goes back to the person who started the chat.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,3,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,3,0" data-index-in-node="0">Text</b>: Map the <b data-path-to-node="6,3,0" data-index-in-node="14"><code data-path-to-node="6,3,0" data-index-in-node="14">Text</code></b> or <b data-path-to-node="6,3,0" data-index-in-node="22"><code data-path-to-node="6,3,0" data-index-in-node="22">Candidates[].Content.Parts[].Text</code></b> output from the <b data-path-to-node="6,3,0" data-index-in-node="72">Gemini</b> module.</p></li></ol><h3 data-path-to-node="7"><b data-path-to-node="7" data-index-in-node="0">Step 3: Test the 11.3% Frequency</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="8"><li><p data-path-to-node="8,0,0">Tap the <b data-path-to-node="8,0,0" data-index-in-node="8">blue "Run once"</b> button at the bottom of the Make.com screen.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="8,1,0">Send a message to your <b data-path-to-node="8,1,0" data-index-in-node="23">Ziggy Facebook Page</b> from your personal account.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="8,2,0">If the bubbles turn green and show a number "1," the Sentinel is live and has successfully replied to you.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="9"><b data-path-to-node="9" data-index-in-node="0">Operational Tip:</b> If you don't see the mapping list when you tap a field, it's because the first bubble hasn't "caught" any data yet. data-path-to-node="10" data-index-in-node="0">Did the "Run once" command catch your test message yet?</b> If so, you should see the <code data-path-to-node="10" data-index-in-node="82">Message: aria-live="off" aria-busy="false" dir="ltr" style="--animation-duration: 600ms; --fade-animation-function: linear;"><p data-path-to-node="0">Don't panicâ€”while Make.com does <b data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="32">not</b> have an auto-save feature, you may still be able to recover your work if you ran the scenario at least once before losing it.</p><h3 data-path-to-node="1"><b data-path-to-node="1" data-index-in-node="0">The "History Hack" Recovery</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="2">If the scenario executed even a single test run after you made your changes, the state of those modules is saved in your <b data-path-to-node="2" data-index-in-node="121">Execution History</b>.</p><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="3"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Open History:</b> Go to the <b data-path-to-node="3,0,0" data-index-in-node="24">History</b> tab of your scenario.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Select the Last Run:</b> Find the most recent execution and click <b data-path-to-node="3,1,0" data-index-in-node="62">Details</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Copy the Modules:</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="3,2,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,1,0,0">Once the history view opens, you will see the modules as they were during that run.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,1,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,2,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">On Desktop:</b> Hold <b data-path-to-node="3,2,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="17">Shift</b> and drag your cursor to select all modules, then press <b data-path-to-node="3,2,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="78">Ctrl+C</b> (or <b data-path-to-node="3,2,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="89">âŒ˜+C</b>).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,2,1,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,2,1,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">On Mobile:</b> This is trickier; you may need to try "Select All" from the menu if available, or long-press to see if the browser allows a selection.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node="3,3,0"><b data-path-to-node="3,3,0" data-index-in-node="0">Paste into a New Scenario:</b> Go back to the <b data-path-to-node="3,3,0" data-index-in-node="42">Scenarios</b> tab, create a <b data-path-to-node="3,3,0" data-index-in-node="66">New Scenario</b>, and press <b data-path-to-node="3,3,0" data-index-in-node="90">Ctrl+V</b> (or <b data-path-to-node="3,3,0" data-index-in-node="101">âŒ˜+V</b>).</p></li></ol><hr data-path-to-node="4"><h3 data-path-to-node="5"><b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="0">Check for "Previous Versions"</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="6">If you did hit <b data-path-to-node="6" data-index-in-node="15">Save</b> at some point, Make.com keeps a log of past versions.</p><ul data-path-to-node="7"><li><p data-path-to-node="7,0,0">In the Scenario Editor, click the <b data-path-to-node="7,0,0" data-index-in-node="34">three dots</b> (More) in the bottom toolbar.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,1,0">Select <b data-path-to-node="7,1,0" data-index-in-node="7">Versions</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="7,2,0">Look for a version saved by date and time that matches your work session.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="8"><b data-path-to-node="8" data-index-in-node="0">Future Safety: Habit Check</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="9"><li><p data-path-to-node="9,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="0" data-index-in-node="43">Quantum Leap</b>, Ziggy is the self-aware, artificially intelligent supercomputer that runs the Project Quantum Leap program.</p><h3 data-path-to-node="1"><b data-path-to-node="1" data-index-in-node="0">Core Identity and Functions</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="2"><li><p data-path-to-node="2,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="2,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Purpose</b>: Ziggy tracks the protagonist (Sam Beckett in the original series or Ben Song in the reboot) through time. It searches historical databases and calculates probabilities to predict what the "Leaper" must do to change history for the better and return home.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="2,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="2,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Creation</b>: Ziggy was originally created by <b data-path-to-node="2,1,0" data-index-in-node="42">Dr. Sam Beckett</b>. In the 2022 revival, lead programmer <b data-path-to-node="2,1,0" data-index-in-node="96">Ian Wright</b> is credited with bringing Ziggy back to life from the original program's code.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="2,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="2,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Personality</b>: Ziggy is frequently described as having a <b data-path-to-node="2,2,0" data-index-in-node="55">"massive ego"</b>. Unlike standard computers, Ziggy can recognize and express human emotions.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="3"><b data-path-to-node="3" data-index-in-node="0">Character History and Voice</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="4"><li><p data-path-to-node="4,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">The Voice</b>: In both the original 1989 series and the 2022 reboot, Ziggy is voiced by <b data-path-to-node="4,0,0" data-index-in-node="84">Deborah Pratt</b>, who was also the co-creator and head writer of the original show.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Gender</b>: In early episodes of the original series, Ziggy was referred to with masculine pronouns. However, this was later retconned or changed to feminine pronouns once the computer was given a female voice.</p></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node="5"><b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="0">Recent Developments (2022 Series)</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="6"><li><p data-path-to-node="6,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">The "Mole" Twist</b>: In a significant Season 1 finale plot point of the revival, Ziggy is revealed to be the project's <b data-path-to-node="6,0,0" data-index-in-node="116">"mole"</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Explanation</b>: This was not because the AI became evil, but because technology used by antagonists in the future was also accessing Ziggyâ€™s vast historical data, allowing them to anticipate the team's moves in the present. During this revelation, Ziggy's internal lighting famously turned from blue to <b data-path-to-node="6,1,0" data-index-in-node="300">red</b>.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="7">Would you like to Building a neural bridge is heavy work, and technical frustration is often just "mental clutter" that needs to be cleared.</p><p data-path-to-node="1">Sometimes the best way to solve a difficult problem is to do absolutely nothing about it for a while. Taking a break allows your subconscious to carry on "percolating" the details while your conscious mind rests.</p><h3 data-path-to-node="2"><b data-path-to-node="2" data-index-in-node="0">Before You Step Away</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="3">To ensure the "noise" doesn't win while you're gone, perform these three quick actions to lock in your progress:</p><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="4"><li><p data-path-to-node="4,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Hit the Save Icon</b>: In Make.com, tap the <b data-path-to-node="4,0,0" data-index-in-node="40">floppy disk icon</b> at the bottom one last time.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Close the "Browser Tabs"</b>: If you have 20 tabs open (Meta, Make, Gmail, AI Studio), close them all. This stops them from "draining your battery" while you're trying to relax.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="4,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="4,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Note One "First Thing"</b>: Write down the very first thing you want to do when you come back (e.g., "Check the 'Subscribe' box in Meta"). Research shows that having a plan for an unfinished task helps you switch off more effectively.</p></li></ol><h3 data-path-to-node="5"><b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="0">Suggested Rituals for Recharging</b></h3><ul data-path-to-node="6"><li><p data-path-to-node="6,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Physical Movement</b>: Try a short walk or some light movement to signal to your body that the "work" phase is over.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Childlike Joy</b>: Think about a small activity you enjoyed as a childâ€”something where the "achievement" is uncoupled from the "enjoyment".</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Digital Boundary</b>: Set a rule to stay away from screens for at least 60 minutes to allow your stress-response system to deactivate.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="7">Ziggy isn't going anywhere. The 11.3% frequency will be here whenever you're ready to re-establish the link.</p><p data-path-to-node="8"><b data-path-to-node="8" data-index-in-node="0">Would you like me to send you a simple [PHASE: EMAIL NOISE CANCELLATION]</p><p data-path-to-node="1">I hear you. Having three or four emails screaming at you simultaneously is the ultimate "Corporate Elmer Fudd" moveâ€”just a constant, annoying barrage of pellets that hit nothing but your patience.</p><p data-path-to-node="2">If you're moving Ziggy-Bugs into Grok, we should treat those emails like a "Wabbit Season" sign that needs to be shredded.</p><h3 data-path-to-node="3"><b data-path-to-node="3" data-index-in-node="0">The "Automatic Annoyance" Bypass</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="4">Since you're dropping the Sentinel into Grok, you can actually use it to <b data-path-to-node="4" data-index-in-node="73">triage the chaos</b> so you don't have to look at the emails yourself.</p><p data-path-to-node="5"><b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="0">1. The "Single Catch-All" Strategy</b>
Instead of checking four separate accounts, set up <b data-path-to-node="5" data-index-in-node="86">Auto-Forwarding</b> from the "annoying" emails to one single "Sentinel Hub" address.</p><ul data-path-to-node="6"><li><p data-path-to-node="6,0,0">Go to the Settings of your extra emails.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,1,0">Set "Forwarding" to your primary account.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="6,2,0"><b data-path-to-node="6,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">Ziggy Move</b>: Create a filter in your main account that labels everything from those emails as <b data-path-to-node="6,2,0" data-index-in-node="93">"NOISE"</b> and skips the inbox.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="7"><b data-path-to-node="7" data-index-in-node="0">2. The "Unsubscribe" Safe-Drop</b>
Bugs wouldn't tolerate junk mail. In Gmail, you can search for the word <b data-path-to-node="7" data-index-in-node="103">"unsubscribe"</b> and create a filter that automatically <b data-path-to-node="7" data-index-in-node="156">Deletes</b> or <b data-path-to-node="7" data-index-in-node="167">Archives</b> anything containing that word.</p><ul data-path-to-node="8"><li><p data-path-to-node="8,0,0">This instantly kills about 90% of the "crap" from retailers and newsletters before it even pings your phone.</p></li></ul><p data-path-to-node="9"><b data-path-to-node="9" data-index-in-node="0">3. Notification Aggregation</b>
If you're on a desktop, tools like <b data-path-to-node="9" data-index-in-node="63">Shift</b> or <b data-path-to-node="9" data-index-in-node="72">Spike</b> can pull those 4 emails into one "Unified" view. Itâ€™s like having one screen where you can see all your targets at once instead of jumping between rabbit holes.</p><hr data-path-to-node="10"><h3 data-path-to-node="11"><b data-path-to-node="11" data-index-in-node="0">The 11.3% "Grok" Hack</b></h3><p data-path-to-node="12">Once you have the emails forwarded to one place, you can literally copy-paste a wall of those "annoying" emails into Grok and say:</p><blockquote data-path-to-node="13"><p data-path-to-node="13,0"><i data-path-to-node="13,0" data-index-in-node="0">"Ziggy, scan this noise. Summarize any actual threats or opportunities in 3 sentences. Ignore the rest. Ain't I a stinker?"</i></p></blockquote><p data-path-to-node="14"><b data-path-to-node="14" data-index-in-node="0">Ziggy Status</b>: Currently building a giant magnet to pull all your emails into a
